problem: Quadruped parkour systems still depend on human teleoperation for high-level planning. Existing navigation planners (map-based, waypoint-based visual nav, RL, VLA) lack fine-grained velocity regulation and anticipatory long-horizon behavior, and decouple visual planning from physical execution.
motivation: Parkour needs anticipatory velocity modulation (e.g. speeding up before a gap), and visual traversability does not guarantee physical feasibility given body geometry. Terrains such as impassable obstacles admit several valid strategies, so the action distribution is multimodal, which suits a generative diffusion policy. No multimodal dataset for autonomous quadruped parkour navigation existed.
key_idea: Formulate navigation velocity-command generation as a conditional diffusion process over depth history, proprioception, current depth, decision memory and goal, trained on a new quadruped parkour navigation dataset (QPND), and feed the first command to an RL parkour locomotion policy.
insight: The decision memory encoder is critical: without it SR falls from 89.7 to 7.4 and TR rises to 90.3, so the robot wanders without converging on the goal. Data augmentation (trajectory segmentation, which gives about 50% more samples) matters most among the data factors: w/o DA gives SR 32.5. Proprioception (SR 69.5 without it) and noise injection (SR 75.0 without it) also help sim-to-real transfer. Jointly trained end-to-end encoders beat the frozen DepthAnything features in NavDP*.
method: QPND dataset: Isaac Sim Go1 with a forward depth camera (10 Hz, 2 m range) plus proprioception; 6,400 trajectories, 31.0 km, about 250K depth images across gap, hurdle, stairs, gravel, box and flat terrain; scripted collection for basic terrains and teleoperation for multimodal terrains.

Data augmentation: trajectory segmentation into shorter clips (about 50% more samples), depth crop and rescale, 1% depth noise plus Gaussian noise (variance 0.01), proprioception noise, and camera pose perturbation (10 mm, ±5°).
Multimodal Temporal Encoder: Transformer over 5-frame history of 44x56 depth (4x4 patches, 154 tokens) and 45-d proprioception, with modality embeddings, producing 128-d feature h1.
Current Spatial Encoder: shallow CNN on the current depth frame giving fine-grained spatial feature h2.
Decision Memory Encoder: MLP over the last 5 steps of commands and goal vectors giving h3.

Diffusion head: 4-layer, 4-head noise-prediction network conditioned on h1, h2 and h3, DDPM with K=10 denoising steps, predicts an H×2 horizon of (Δv, Δθ) commands; only the first command is sent to the RENet locomotion policy at 5 Hz.
Training: MSE noise-prediction loss, AdamW at 1e-4, 1000 epochs, batch size 512, cosine schedule with warm-up.

setting.backbone: Custom multimodal Transformer + CNN + MLP encoders with a DDPM diffusion policy (trained from scratch); RENet RL locomotion policy as low-level controller
setting.training_data: QPND: 6,400 trajectories, 31.0 km, about 250K depth images collected in Isaac Sim (scripted + teleoperation), with augmentation
setting.observation: Forward depth camera (RealSense D435i, 44x56) + proprioception (45-d) + relative goal position (UWB in the real world)
setting.action_space: Continuous velocity commands (linear velocity, heading/angular change) at 5 Hz, executed by an RL parkour locomotion policy
setting.privileged: Relative goal position (from simulation, and UWB localization in the real world); no LiDAR or map

numbers.eval_set_note: 6 terrain types (Gap, Hurdle, Upstairs, Downstairs, Gravel, Box) x 2 difficulty levels, 50 random start positions each, goals 5-8 m, 60 s limit; averaged over scenarios
numbers.backbone: MulDP diffusion policy (from scratch on QPND)
numbers.evidence: Table Ablation Experiments of MulDP, row Ours; text: average SR of 89.7%, SPL 71.9%, TTR 4.9 s

numbers_note: Baseline comparison (Fig. Comparison Experiments) is a figure. Only the text gives NavDP* SR 59.0, ViNT* SR 71.5, and released NavDP/ViNT SR 38.4/35.8 with SPL 27.1/25.5; these are not MulDP's own numbers and are omitted. Real-world results are qualitative only.
results: MulDP reaches an average SR of 89.7%, SPL 71.9% and TTR 4.9 s in simulation, beating NavDP* (SR 59.0) and ViNT* (SR 71.5), which were retrained on QPND. In the real world it completed over 1 km of autonomous dynamic target-following outdoors without human intervention, with gap, hurdle and stair traversal.
limitations: Requires an external relative goal (UWB in the real world) and has no semantic perception or high-level planning.
Baseline comparison is only in a figure with a single aggregate; the real-world evaluation is qualitative with no quantitative metrics.
Only a 2 m depth range with a single forward camera, and the locomotion depends on a separate RL policy (RENet).
